slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.brief: Light of two different wavelengths incident on the same metal; use Einstein's photoelectric equation to relate stopping potentials and find the work function or the maximum KE ratio for the two wavelengths.

stem: For a metal, light of wavelengths $400\ \text{nm}$ and $800\ \text{nm}$ gives stopping potentials in the ratio $3:1$. Taking $hc=1240\ \text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$, find the work function of the metal.

verdicts.working: Photon energies are 1240/400 = 3.10 eV and 1240/800 = 1.55 eV. Thus (3.10 − φ)/(1.55 − φ) = 3, giving φ = 0.775 eV.

working:
$K_1/K_2=3$; $E_1=1240/400=3.10\ \text{eV}$, $E_2=1240/800=1.55\ \text{eV}$. $(3.10-\phi)/(1.55-\phi)=3\Rightarrow\phi=0.775\ \text{eV}$.

Independent check: Photon energies are 1240/400 = 3.10 eV and 1240/800 = 1.55 eV. Thus (3.10 − φ)/(1.55 − φ) = 3, giving φ = 0.775 eV.
